selection: FinanceBench selected for a small non-coding document-QA domain before downloading or inspecting its response table. Metadata contain 150 items and 16 model/context configurations, public binary item-level responses. No score was used for selection.
motivation: Earlier public-data acquisition diagnostics found squared-bias costs of Beta(1,1) in low-success groups. The four already inspected benchmarks are development data; private formative feedback is not used for parameter selection.
comparison: Fixed Beta(0.5,0.5) versus fixed Beta(1,1), empirical mean and constant 0.5 on identical pools and acquired responses. No fitting, search, adaptive acquisition or new leaderboard submission.
eligibility: Include every complete visible-subject group with >=80 distinct observed items. All source groups have at most 150 items. Exclude missing grades, retain repeated response rows and report infeasible pools or ineligible groups without replacing the benchmark based on outcomes.
endpoint: Primary: macro mean paired observed Brier ALC, Beta(0.5,0.5) minus Beta(1,1), averaged over the three acquisition seeds and all eligible FinanceBench groups. Lower is better. Seeds share evaluation pools and are not independent benchmarks.
decision_rule: Support an overall advantage on this benchmark only if primary observed and exact conditional expected ALC are both lower than Beta(1,1), observed ALC is lower than empirical mean, the average observed Brier at budgets 1 and 3 remains below empirical mean, and the near-duplicate sensitivity does not reverse the direction. Otherwise report a tradeoff or negative result, without adjusting alpha or changing the validation benchmark.
diagnostics: Report all budgets and seed differences. Evaluate the prespecified evaluation-success-rate <0.1 slice using weighted exact squared bias and expected ALC. This outcome-defined slice is retrospective and never a prediction-time feature. If empty, report the question as untested on the new benchmark. Development diagnostics are reported separately, including size 80-1000 and all-group populations.
expectation: Exact over uniform acquisition-item sampling without replacement and one uniform recorded response per acquired item, conditional on fixed acquisition/evaluation pools; not over new items, new splits or new benchmarks.
limitations: One new public benchmark; no private-test or benchmark-generalization claim.
No statistical significance claim or confidence interval from the three dependent acquisition seeds.
Models may recur across benchmarks: this tests new benchmark items, not unseen model identities.
Lexical grouping does not guarantee semantic or document-level independence; no item-text features are fitted.
All acquired labels belong to the same eight-field subject configuration and benchmark alias; no evaluation labels enter prediction.
Exact expectations and success-rate slices use outcomes only for retrospective analysis.
The complete-group size filter does not reproduce official balanced packing under the 1000-pair cap.
Source data and private formative feedback are not redistributed.
